title: Shot manifest (shots.json)
description: Every shot of one episode, in order, as one continuous film. A shot is one unbroken camera idea with a start state and an end state; the next shot starts where this one ends. How to plan and fill it: films/channels/studio/SHOTS.md. Checked by films/channels/studio/tools/validate.py together with episode.json (episode.schema.json). Keys that start with 'x-' are free for a channel's own notes.

episode.description: The id in the episode's episode.json.

journey.description: Optional. One or two sentences: the whole camera path, start to end.

continuity.description: Optional. What stays the same in every shot of this episode: light direction, the one skin tone, the spine readout's place, the screen direction of travel.

shots.description: In order. Windows start at 0, do not overlap, leave no gap, and end at the episode's planned length.

transition.description: One term from the transition vocabulary in SHOTS.md, then optionally ': ' and the detail. A shot's transitionOut and the next shot's transitionIn describe the same join and use the same term.

id.description: S01, S02 ... in order. A shot added later between two takes a letter: S04a.

beat.description: Optional. The story beat (script.md heading) this shot belongs to. Letters, digits and underscores only, as in episode.json.

purpose.description: Why the shot exists: what the viewer must understand or feel by its last frame. A shot with no purpose is cut.

seconds.description: [start, end] in seconds on the episode's clock. A plan until the voice is measured; then the compile step's word anchors replace it.

aspect.description: The episode's aspect. A 16:9 film and its 9:16 parts each get their own manifest and their own framing.

preset.description: A camera preset name from SHOTS.md (for example locked, keyed-flight, mount-drift), so the builder knows which code to use.

from.description: Where the camera is and what it looks at on the first frame.

to.description: The same for the last frame. Equal to 'from' for a locked shot.

lens.description: Field of view in degrees, and what is in focus. The engine takes a field of view, not a lens in millimetres.

focus.description: Optional. What the focus follows, and any pull.

speed.description: Optional. How fast the move is, in the channel's own limits.

subject.description: The one thing the eye is on. One line wins.

motion.description: What moves in the world (not the camera), and on which spoken word it lands.

lighting.description: The light in this shot, named with what the code offers today (SHOTS.md, lighting presets). Anything not built yet is marked 'to build'.

environment.description: The place: ground, depth, atmosphere, particles.

materials.description: What things are made of, named with real materials and passes (SHOTS.md, material presets).

principle.description: The science this shot shows, in one or two plain sentences. It must match the claims listed.

startState.description: The first frame, described so the previous shot's endState can be checked against it.

endState.description: The last frame. The next shot's startState picks it up.

narration.description: The lines spoken during the shot: line ids (vo01), or the id and the text. Empty for a picture-only shot.

sound.description: Music level, foley and any sound event, in the channel's sound rules.

assets.description: Paths the shot needs: code modules, art, references, recordings. May be empty while planning.

claims.description: Ids in the episode's claims.json that this shot's picture or narration states. Empty when the shot states nothing outside the film.

qa.description: Acceptance checks for this shot: things a person or a script can answer yes or no.

status.description: planned: on paper. built: rendered at least as stills. approved: the owner or reviewer accepted it.

onScreenText.description: Optional. Any word or number on screen besides the captions.

aiArt.description: Optional. True when an AI-made image appears in this shot's picture. Then the episode's disclosures.aiVisuals must be true.

reference.description: Optional. Path to a reference frame the builder matches. A reference is not shown in the film.
